label: r3c2
name: flip, 1 epoch, 64 minibatches
hypothesis: Change: ppo_epochs 1 as in the first candidate, plus n_minibatches 64 (64 samples per minibatch). This keeps about 426k steps and doubles the gradient steps per sample. Why: one epoch with 32 minibatches gives slightly fewer optimiser steps than r2c1, so the agent might gain samples but lose fitting. Refuted if this scores below the 1-epoch, 32-minibatch candidate by more than the seed noise of about 6 points, or below 0.90.
last_analysis: Two changes account for almost all of the progress. The x-flip before the head fixed the mirrored action mapping (0 to 0.75). Fewer PPO epochs, which buys more samples, raised success further: 3 epochs gave 0.79, 2 gave 0.90, 1 gave 0.92, and 1 epoch with 64 minibatches gave 0.96 (best, seeds 0.97 and 0.95). Several ideas did not help: learned axis mixing (0.04), global context added to the head (0.78), the dilated conv (0.72) and gamma 0.99 (0.82, within noise of its comparison). Seed noise is about 2 to 6 points. r3c2's training success stops rising at about 0.90 by 75% of training with the entropy coefficient at 0.03. That suggests more learning per sample (higher learning rate) or less exploration noise. The remaining errors are a few cells placed outside the target, which suggests the head sometimes misjudges landing layers. Raw per-column layer features passed straight to the head may fix that.
